primary_sources.title: Friedhelm Waldhausen, On irreducible 3-manifolds which are sufficiently large, Ann.Math.87(1968),56-88
primary_sources.used_statement: Theorem6.1, printed page77 / PDF page23: an injective map of pairs between irreducible boundary-irreducible 3-manifolds, with sufficiently large target, is homotopic to a covering except for the specified product-line-bundle alternative. Applied to a peripheral pi1 isomorphism, excluding that alternative by boundary count, to obtain a degree-one covering. The page was rendered and visually inspected.

primary_sources.title: Walter Neumann, A calculus for plumbing applied to the topology of complex surface singularities and degenerating complex curves, Trans AMS268(1981),299-344
primary_sources.used_statement: Proposition2.1 R6 in both closed and punctured versions; Theorem6.1(III) linear-chain lens spaces. The already visually audited R6 has one remaining branch, zero removed punctures and no extra summands.

primary_sources.title: Allen Hatcher, Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology
primary_sources.used_statement: Propositions1.11-1.13: horizontal/vertical incompressible surfaces in Seifert manifolds, irreducibility and boundary incompressibility; Corollary3.9 asphericity; retained compression and loop-theorem inputs. Disk base with two cones is atoroidal by these statements.

primary_sources.title: Peter Scott, The geometries of 3-manifolds, Bull. London Math. Soc.15(1983),401-487
primary_sources.used_statement: Sections2-3: Seifert presentations and regular-fiber slopes, Euler number and finite cover scaling. Used with the retained separately proved ordinary branch extension.

primary_sources.used_statement: Retained Section2 cable-space fiber and peripheral slopes. Winding p here and signed a are kept in the actual boundary lattice.
